dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. Good afternoon.
Hi? Yes, good afternoon? I'm calling about a storm drain? It's, um, it's gurgling? And there's a smell coming up out of it, like a sewer smell?
Oh, okay. A gurgling storm drain with a sewer smell. Let me get some details from you. Where is the drain, do you have a street address or a corner?
Well, I'd rather not give the number on the phone? I'm just, I'm a landlord and it's near my tenants? Can I tell you it's on the corner by the little seawall, where the street dead-ends at the water?
I do need a street name to put on the work order. Can you tell me the street, even without a house number?
Oh. Oh, I see? Okay, um, hold on, I'm sorry, I'm wearing my glasses on my head? It's, uh, the end of Wilbur Avenue? Right where the pavement stops at the water?
Wilbur Avenue, the dead end by the water. Got it. And the drain is right at the end of the pavement?
Yes? Right at the edge? It's the one with the iron grate? It was fine before the storm? The one that ended Saturday? And now it makes this gurgling noise, like a bathtub? And then the smell comes up?
Okay. So the coastal storm that ended Saturday, three days ago, and since then it gurgles and smells. Is there any water standing in the street around it right now?
A little? There's a puddle that doesn't go away? It was there this morning when my tenant went out? She said it's still there?
A puddle that's stayed since the storm. Is it coming up out of the drain, or just sitting around it?
I think it's coming up? Or maybe it's just the tide? I really can't tell, I'm not down there myself, I'm only going by what she tells me?
That's fine, that's helpful either way. Any damage to a building that you know of? Water in a basement or anything like that?

No, no, thank goodness? Nothing like that? It's the other part that worries me? There are kids who walk down that way to the water, after school? And people with dogs, all the time? And if that's sewage, I don't know, is it safe? Should they be near it?

I understand. I'd say people should keep kids and dogs away from standing water near a drain like that until someone looks at it. I'll note on the order that there's foot traffic at the end of the street, so the crew knows it's a concern.
Oh, thank you? Would you do that? Because it's getting dark so early now? And nobody can see the puddle?

Yes, I'll put it in. Let me read back what I have. Wilbur Avenue, at the dead end by the water, storm drain with an iron grate, gurgling, sewer odor, standing water since Saturday's storm, kids and dog walkers use the area. Is that right?
Yes? That's it exactly? You're very thorough?
Thank you. Now, I'll want a number in case the crew needs to reach someone. What's a good one for you?
Four oh one, five five five, oh one five one. Is that a landline? Will someone pick up in the evening?

It is, yes? I'm usually here. Although, I'm sorry, earlier today I was on a video call with my sister for ages? And it wore my battery down on the cell phone? So I'm using the house phone, which is why I'm calling so late in the day?
No problem at all, the house phone works fine for us. I'll put that number down.
Good? So, will there be a work order opened? And do you know what date someone would come out?

Yes, I'm opening the work order right now as we talk. As for the date, crews are working through a long list after the storm, so I'd say it could be a few days to a week or so. I'll mark it as a possible sewer odor, which gets looked at sooner than a plain puddle.
A week? Oh, dear? Is there anything I should tell the tenants in the meantime? Just stay away?

Yes, keep the kids and dogs back from it, and don't walk through the water. If it gets worse, say the water rises up into the street or the smell gets stronger, call us right back and we'll bump it up.
Okay? I'll tell her tonight? Could I get a number for the work order? In case I need to ask about it?

Sure. Give me a second, it's generating. [pause] Okay, the system has it as a request under storm drain, Wilbur Avenue, dated today, Tuesday the thirteenth. When you call, just say that, and any of us can pull it up.
Tuesday the thirteenth, Wilbur Avenue, storm drain? Okay? I'll write that on my pad?
Perfect. Anything else I can help with this afternoon, Mrs. Gifford?
No, I think that's everything? Thank you so much, dear? You've been very patient?
You're welcome. Take care, and stay warm tonight.
You too? Goodbye?
